sources.content:
#### Python Update

This Fusion release updates the Python version from 3.12 to 3.14. Besides the API, Fusion uses Python for a few other things, and this Python update includes security fixes. Most people won’t notice any change. Those affected are the developers and users of any Python apps delivered as .pyc files. Previous versions of these add-ins will be broken because .pyc files are tied to the minor version of Python that was used to create them. Add-ins compiled with the current version (3.12) will not be compatible with the new release (3.14) and will fail to load. This change does not affect any add-ins where the .py source code is available.

sources.title: Node.js LTS Schedule: Current vs Active vs Maintenance
sources.content:
## The short answer

Run an LTS line in production. Today that means Node.js 24, in Active LTS until 20 October 2026 and supported until 30 April 2028, or Node.js 22, already in Maintenance and supported until 30 April 2027. Node.js 26 becomes LTS on 28 October 2026 and is supported until 30 April 2029. Node.js 20 reached end of life on 30 April 2026. From Node.js 27, the project ships one major release a year instead of two, every major becomes LTS, and a new Alpha channel replaces the odd-numbered releases for early testing.

Want the end dates in one table? Node.js end-of-life dates lists 18, 20, 22, 24 and 26, checked against endoflife.date on 20 October 2026.

## The three phases: Current, Active LTS and Maintenance [...] ## Which Node.js version should you run?

 New services: Node.js 24 today, or 26 once it becomes LTS on 28 October 2026 if your dependencies support it. 26 gives a year more runway, to 30 April 2029.
 Services on Node.js 22: you are in Maintenance, with security fixes until 30 April 2027. Plan the move to 24 or 26 now rather than in the spring.
 Services on Node.js 20 or older: you have no upstream security fixes. Upgrade, or cover the runtime while you do. Our Node.js 18 and 20 to 22 and 24 upgrade guide walks through the breaking changes.
 Library authors: from October 2026, add the Node.js 27 Alpha to CI. The project specifically asks for it, so bugs surface before they reach users on LTS.

#### What is the latest Node.js LTS version?

Node.js 24 is the Active LTS line (EOL April 30, 2028) and Node.js 22 is in Maintenance LTS (EOL April 30, 2027). Node.js 26, released in May 2026, is the Current line and is scheduled to enter LTS in October 2026.

#### Why should I avoid odd-numbered Node.js versions in production?

Odd-numbered releases (19, 21, 23, 25) never enter LTS. They stay Current for six months and then go straight to EOL, so they receive no long-term security support. Use even-numbered LTS lines for production.
